newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends softer on renewed inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends softer on renewed inflation fears.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended softer on Wednesday at C$1.3974 (US$0.7156) from Tuesday's close at C$1.3965 (US$0.7160) on renewed speculation over the state of U.S. inflation.
* Traders said the currency eased in relatively quiet trading after the U.S. reported higher than expected industrial production in March.

The higher manufacturing and industrial output numbers renewed speculation that inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy would encourage the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in May.

"Demand is vigorous, shelves are empty, and this will continue to push existing capacity pressure," said Kevin Flanagan, money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. "This will definitely capture the Fed's attention."
Traders said renewed speculation about a rise would continue to pressure the Canadian dollar.
On March 25, the Federal Reserve raised U.S. rates by 25 basis points for the first time since 1995, widening the spread between short-term Canadian and U.S. debt yields.
The wider spreads led international investors to sell off their Canadian dollar holdings over the last month for a richer interest payment from U.S. debt instruments.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 1.2370 marks from Tuesday's close of 1.2309 marks, but fell to 90.03 yen from Tuesday's 90.19 yen.
